problem: VLN agents are trained on coarse-grained instruction-trajectory pairs, which give only weak cross-modal alignment supervision between instruction sub-phrases and trajectory segments or landmarks.
motivation: Precise alignment between instruction and predicted trajectory is one of the most critical challenges in VLN. Fine-grained, human-annotated alignment data could supply the missing supervision and improve training components that depend on data characteristics.
key_idea: Introduce Landmark-RxR, a human-annotated fine-grained VLN dataset, and use it to redesign data augmentation, training paradigm, reward shaping, navigation loss and evaluation for better cross-modal alignment.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that fine-grained alignment data effectively improves the agent's cross-modal alignment ability across the components studied.
method: Landmark-RxR dataset: human-annotated fine-grained VLN data providing precise alignment supervision between instruction parts and trajectories (built on RxR).
Data augmentation: methods designed to exploit the fine-grained data (details not given in abstract).
Training paradigm: a training scheme designed around fine-grained supervision (details not given in abstract).
Reward shaping: rewards designed using the fine-grained alignment (details not given in abstract).
Navigation loss design: losses using fine-grained alignment supervision (details not given in abstract).
Novel evaluation mechanism: a new way to assess alignment (details not given in abstract).

setting.training_data: Landmark-RxR fine-grained human-annotated data (scale not stated in abstract)
setting.simulator: not specified in abstract (3D indoor VLN environments)

results: The abstract reports only qualitatively that fine-grained data effectively improves the agent's cross-modal alignment ability. No numbers or baselines are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative details and limitations could not be assessed.
